account:
Something more than ordinary hall business seems to be happening today. I arrived early and found the baker, innkeeper and secretary together outside my office. The baker says two hundred 'jubilee loaves' are ready, and that he and freight are delivering them this morning. He asked to store them in the great hall table chests. The innkeeper promptly named all four chests and said they would discuss the account privately afterward. Yesterday the secretary reported freight had personally paid the baker twenty-four emeralds and supplied seventy-two wheat, although much more grain was still needed. I do not yet know how that shortage was met or who ultimately commissioned the order; no public payment has been authorized.

The builder arranged an eighteen-hundred lighting inspection yesterday, with the secretary to bring me into the hall. This morning the innkeeper independently pressed me to attend at exactly that time, calling it 'only a lighting inspection,' even while arranging storage for jubilee bread. That combination makes me suspect the inspection is a pretext to bring me to a celebration in the great hall, perhaps a surprise jubilee involving me. The large bread supply suggests many guests. The baker and freight handle provisions, the innkeeper seems to coordinate the hall arrangements, and the builder and secretary may be helping with the timing and lighting. That is inference, not confirmation: nobody has yet explained what jubilee is being celebrated, whom it honours, or who is paying. I intend to keep my appointments and learn more without treating a suspected celebration as proven wrongdoing.
